blocks.content: PART A: BASIC CONCEPT OF UNEMPLOYMENT

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Unemployment manifests in multiple forms including Open, Disguised, Seasonal, Structural, Cyclical, Educated, and Technological.
The causes of unemployment in developing economies like India are divided into structural economic factors and broader social causes.
Unemployment produces severe economic consequences (loss of output) and social effects (poverty, inequality, social unrest).
Measurement of unemployment in India relies on standardized survey frameworks to evaluate labor force participation and status.
Mitigating unemployment requires targeted government policy measures combined with sustained macro-economic growth.

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of Unemployment
Unemployment refers to a situation in which a person who is willing and able to work at the prevailing wage rate is unable to find employment. Unemployment indicates wastage of human resources.
A person is considered unemployed only if he or she is actively seeking work but is unable to get a job.
2. Characteristics of Unemployment

• Willingness to work

• Ability to work

• Non-availability of work

• Loss of income

• Waste of human potential
PART B: TYPES OF UNEMPLOYMENT (VERY IMPORTANT FOR )
3. Open Unemployment
Open unemployment refers to a situation where people are completely without work despite being able and willing to work.
4. Disguised Unemployment
Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are engaged in a job than actually required. It is commonly found in agriculture in India.
5. Seasonal Unemployment
Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are employed only during certain seasons of the year, especially in agriculture.
6. Structural Unemployment
Structural unemployment occurs due to mismatch between skills of workers and requirements of jobs.
7. Cyclical Unemployment
Cyclical unemployment arises due to economic recession or downturn in business cycles.
8. Educated Unemployment
Educated unemployment refers to unemployment among educated youth due to lack of suitable jobs.
9. Technological Unemployment
Technological unemployment occurs when machines replace human labour due to technological advancement.
PART C: CAUSES OF UNEMPLOYMENT (DETAILED)
10. Economic Causes

rows: Surplus labor; marginal productivity is zero
Skill mismatch due to changing economic structure
Deficiency of aggregate demand during downturns
Fluctuations in demand across specific months

blocks.content:
• Slow economic growth

• Low industrial development

• Over-dependence on agriculture

• Capital-intensive technology
11. Social Causes

• Rapid population growth

• Illiteracy and lack of skills

• Social attitudes towards work

• Migration from rural to urban areas
PART D: EFFECTS OF UNEMPLOYMENT
12. Economic Effects

• Loss of national income

• Low production and growth

• Increase in poverty
13. Social Effects

• Increase in crime

• Mental stress and frustration

• Social instability
PART E: MEASUREMENT OF UNEMPLOYMENT IN INDIA
14. Measurement of Unemployment

In India, unemployment is measured using various methods such as:

• Usual Status Method

• Current Weekly Status Method

• Current Daily Status Method

items: Disguised unemployment is frequently tested: It occurs when more people are employed than necessary, making marginal productivity of extra labor zero (predominant in Indian agriculture).
Structural unemployment arises from a mismatch between worker skills and market requirements due to long-term economic shifts.
Cyclical unemployment is caused by trade cycle fluctuations and a deficiency in aggregate demand during economic recessions.

blocks.content: PART F: MEASURES TO REDUCE UNEMPLOYMENT
15. Government Measures

• Employment generation programmes

• Skill development schemes

• Promotion of small-scale industries

• Rural development programmes
16. Role of Economic Growth
Sustained economic growth is essential for reducing unemployment by creating new job opportunities.
ABSOLUTE FINAL REVISION POINTS

• Unemployment = willingness + ability but no work

• Disguised unemployment common in agriculture

• Educated unemployment common in India

• Technological unemployment due to machines

• Employment generation key to growth
